analysis.one_liner: Raises the federal minimum wage from $5.15 to $6.15 an hour in two steps.
analysis.headline: The bill never got a vote in the Senate HELP Committee and died when the 106th Congress ended; a minimum wage increase eventually became law in 2000 through separate legislation.
analysis.plain_summary: This bill would have raised the federal minimum wage from $5.15 an hour to $5.65 starting September 1, 1999, and then to $6.15 starting September 1, 2000. It also would have applied federal minimum wage rules to the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, which had been exempt. It was referred to the Senate labor committee and never came up for a vote before the Congress ended.
analysis.who_benefits: Workers earning the federal minimum wage would have gotten a $1.00-per-hour raise in two steps, to $6.15 by September 2000. Workers in the Northern Mariana Islands would have gained federal minimum wage protections for the first time.

how_it_helps.text: It would have raised the federal minimum wage from $5.15 to $5.65 an hour starting September 1, 1999, and to $6.15 an hour starting September 1, 2000.
It would have extended federal minimum wage protections to the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, which had previously been exempt.

analysis.who_pays: Employers who pay minimum-wage workers — largely retailers, restaurants, and other labor-intensive businesses — would bear the cost of the higher wage, and some of it may have been passed to consumers through prices.

drawbacks.text: Critics argued a federally mandated wage increase raises costs for small businesses and could reduce entry-level hiring, particularly in low-wage regions and industries like restaurants and retail.

The bill also applied the federal minimum wage to the Northern Mariana Islands, ending a long-standing exemption that had allowed garment manufacturing there to pay below-federal wages — a change that island employers opposed.

analysis.benefit_vs_cost: The benefit was a raise for millions of the lowest-paid workers; the cost was modest and fell on employers of minimum-wage labor, with some economists cautioning about reduced entry-level hiring. The bill died without a vote, so the cost was never tested; the practical result was that low-wage workers got nothing from this bill.

outcome.mechanism: It was sent to the Senate labor committee the day it was introduced, the committee never voted on it, and it died when the 106th Congress ended in January 2001.

narrative.text: Introduced January 19, 1999 with 22 Democratic senators on board, the bill was read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
After the referral, the only further record action was a repeat of the sponsor's introductory remarks on July 24, 2000; the committee never reported the bill and the Senate never voted on it.
No version of this bill received a floor vote in either chamber before the 106th Congress ended.

outcome.who_came_out_ahead: Employers of minimum-wage workers avoided the mandated raise; low-wage workers gained nothing from this bill, though a minimum wage increase was enacted separately later in 2000.

for.name: Sen. Edward M. Kennedy
for.what_they_did: Introduced the bill and delivered introductory remarks at introduction and again in July 2000.

against.name: Senate HELP Committee
against.what_they_did: Took no action on the bill after referral; never reported it to the full Senate.

sides.party_line_note: The sponsor and all 26 cosponsors were Democrats; no Republican sponsored the bill, and the Republican-run Senate committee it was sent to never acted on it.

industries.note: They would have paid higher wages to their lowest-paid staff, raising labor costs in industries that rely on minimum-wage workers. Some small businesses argued the mandate was unaffordable.

industries.industry: Garment manufacturers in the Northern Mariana Islands
industries.note: The bill ended the exemption that allowed factories in the CNMI to pay below-federal wages, which had made the islands a haven for low-cost garment production.
